reply_text:
I read this as a **pass**. The quote is word for word in Meta's own call transcript, and all four parts of the rule hold. Part 2 is the closest call, though I don't think it's borderline.

**Does the quote appear on the page?** Yes, exactly. The PDF is Meta's own transcript of its second-quarter 2022 earnings call, dated July 27th, 2022. In Zuckerberg's prepared remarks it reads: "Right now, about 15% of content in a person's Facebook feed and a little more than that of their Instagram feed is recommended by our AI from people, groups, or accounts that you don't follow. We expect these numbers to more than double by the end of next year." The only difference is a doubled space in the candidate's copy. The transcript comes from the company itself, not a news report, so it is not coverage only.

**The four parts:**
1. **Role: pass.** On 2022-07-27 he was founder and chief executive of Meta Platforms, which had that name from October 2021. Meta was running Facebook AI Research then. The two recorded claims from 2016 and 2018 show the ledger already treats him as qualifying before Llama.
2. **Looks forward and is about AI: pass.** He predicts that more of each feed will be "recommended by our AI", which is about how widely an AI system is used, not about revenue or spending. It sits near the business-forecast line because the next sentences talk about making money from it. But the number being forecast is the AI's share of the feed, not revenue or spending.
3. **Has a date: pass.** "By the end of next year", said in 2022, means 2023-12-31.
4. **Primary source: pass.** The company's own transcript.

**Already recorded?** No. None of his recorded claim files is from 2022 or about how much of the feed the AI recommends.

For whoever writes the test: "more than double" from about 15% (Facebook) and a bit more (Instagram) means over about 30% on Facebook and over twice the Instagram starting figure. Only Meta holds those numbers, so any evidence would be the maker's own figures and should be marked that way.
